package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of Nexus Repository Manager 3 contain CVE-2019-7238, a remote code execution vulnerability. This flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the REST API. While the package itself is not intentionally malicious, the vulnerability enables attackers to inject and run malicious code, making affected versions highly dangerous if left unpatched.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the server processes a crafted HTTP POST request to the /service/rest/beta/repositories endpoint
execution_context.file_location: REST API endpoint handler (vulnerable Java class in NXRM 3 core, typically org.sonatype.nexus.repository.rest.RepositoryApiResource)
required_permissions: filesystem (to create or modify files as a result of command execution)
process_execution (to invoke system commands via java.lang.Runtime)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP POST request to the /service/rest/beta/repositories endpoint with a malicious payload that exploits a Java Expression Language (EL) injection vulnerability, such as: { "name": "test", "online": true, "storage": { "blobStoreName": "default", "strictContentTypeValidation": true }, "format": "maven2", "type": "hosted", "attributes": { "repository": { "content": "${''.getClass().forName('java.lang.Runtime').getRuntime().exec('touch /tmp/pwned')}" } } }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This payload leverages the Java EL injection vulnerability in the REST API. When the server processes the malicious JSON, it evaluates the EL expression, causing the server to execute arbitrary system commands (e.g., creating a file /tmp/pwned) with the privileges of the NXRM process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system commands on the server by injecting Java EL expressions into API input, which is a critical security risk and a hallmark of remote code execution vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API usage should never evaluate user-supplied input as code or allow invocation of system-level commands. User input should be strictly validated and treated as data, not executable expressions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for evaluating user-supplied data as Java code or EL expressions in this context. REST APIs should not permit dynamic code execution based on client input.
key_indicators: Presence of Java EL expressions (e.g., ${...}) in user-supplied JSON fields
API input leading to invocation of java.lang.Runtime.exec() or similar methods
Creation of files or execution of system commands not associated with normal repository management operations
Unusual or malformed JSON payloads targeting the /service/rest/beta/repositories endpoint

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and sends a malicious HTTP POST request to the /service/rest/beta/repositories endpoint, exploiting the EL injection vulnerability in the REST API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the server, enabling actions such as file creation, malware installation, or data exfiltration with the privileges of the NXRM process.

behavioral_signatures: System command execution (e.g., process creation) triggered immediately after REST API requests to /service/rest/beta/repositories
Creation of files (such as /tmp/pwned) or other artifacts not associated with normal repository operations
Detection of Java EL expressions (e.g., ${...}) or references to java.lang.Runtime in JSON payloads sent to the REST API
Unusual or malformed JSON structures in POST requests to /service/rest/beta/repositories
file_indicators: /tmp/pwned or other files created by attacker-supplied commands
Unexpected scripts or binaries appearing on the server after API requests
network_indicators: Inbound POST requests to /service/rest/beta/repositories containing suspicious or EL-injected JSON payloads
Outbound network connections initiated by the server following API requests, potentially as a result of executed commands
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor REST API endpoints, especially /service/rest/beta/repositories, for suspicious or malformed JSON payloads containing Java EL expressions or references to java.lang.Runtime. Audit server logs for unexpected file creation, process execution, or outbound network activity following API requests. Deploy file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in the filesystem. Ensure all NXRM instances are updated to version 3.15 or later to eliminate the vulnerability.
